answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register by burning cryptographic stake that scales quadratically with identity count, imposing superlinear cost C(k)=b*k^2. As an attacker attempts a gale of clone registrations to capture consensus, the marginal burn drives their net profit to an absolute nadir. While a single honest participant comfortably stakes on a low cost knoll, malicious swarms face exponential economic friction.
